column1: # gates/baseline.tsv — the ratchet baseline (deterministic-gates §6).
# Seeded for a new context compiler: one row per shipped gate, all at zero,
# because a fresh compiler has no violations yet. A gate that arrives RED gets
# disabled by lunchtime; a gate that records the truth holds the line from here.
# Format: <gate_id><TAB><command><TAB><violations><TAB><suppressions><TAB><recorded_at><TAB><note>
# The command must support --count, printing "<violations>TAB<suppressions>"
# and exiting 0. A command that exits 2 fails the ratchet as a gate error —
# never as a pass.
# SUPPRESSIONS ARE VIOLATIONS. A scope_exclude on a rule, a declared standalone,
# a nolint pragma — each counts in the second number. Routing around a gate
# moves a watched number, so it can never be the quiet option.
# WHEN /ctx-gate BUILDS A GATE it adds a row here with the REAL violation count
# from its whole-repo scan — not 0. Recording 0 when the repo has 12 makes the
# gate red on arrival; recording 12 means the rule holds from now on without
# requiring the past to be fixed first.
# TO LOWER A NUMBER: fix the violations, then edit the row. Downward is silent.
# TO RAISE ONE: edit deliberately and say why in the note. That edit is the
# record of the decision.
# gate_id
